Pairing moves into Settings and looks the same as in KnightLoader: the two tiles open windows, one showing the twelve words with a Copy button and one taking them with a Paste button, and the Fleet tab becomes the Instances tab with each instance's address on its card. Pairing works without a login password now, with a plain warning until one is set. Two instances on one network without a relay stay paired, and a config-only container backup shows its date on the dashboard again.

## 🎨 Changed

### Pairing

- **Pairing is on the System tab of Settings**, next to the login password, with the instance name below it. The Instances page keeps a **Pairing** button that takes you there, and a link to the old Pairing tab under Instances goes there too.
- **Generate phrase opens a window with the twelve words** and a Copy button. **Enter phrase** opens a window with the field, twelve numbered slots and a **Paste** button that reads the words from the clipboard. Where the browser does not allow that, for example over plain HTTP, the window says to paste into the field by hand.
- **The member list starts with this instance**, marked This instance, followed by every member with Direct or Via relay. Every row has the same height.
- **A group that stays alone for a minute offers two tiles**: show the words again to enter them on the other instance, or enter the other instance's words and join its group in one step. The two-step hint with Leave group is gone.
- **When the relay can't be reached, the card says so in one line**, with **What to check** for the list and **Check again**.
- **The relay card says No group yet** until this instance has a phrase, since the relay only connects inside a group.
- **Pairing works without a login password.** Generating, entering and showing the phrase no longer need one. Until a password is set, the phrase card warns that anyone who can open the web interface can read the words and, through the group, get the restic password of every instance in it. Its **Set password** button jumps to the password field. With a password set, showing the phrase again still asks for it.

### Instances

- **The Fleet tab is now the Instances tab** and comes first. Each card shows the address that instance answers on.
- **Before there is a group, the tab is one large Pairing tile** that leads to Settings. Once there is one, the **Pairing** button sits below the cards.

### Dashboard

- **The badges in the protection rows stay on one line.** Their columns take the longest badge on any row, and the schedule text shortens instead. The off-site DR result sits on the line below, next to its button, and in a narrow window each row stacks its badges.

### Self-backup and Flash

- **The learning caption of anomaly detection sits in the backup card**, beside the Backup button, instead of on its own above the page.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Two instances on the same network without a relay no longer drop out of their group** after a few minutes ([#270](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/270)). An instance found by its address counted as reachable for five minutes, and only opening the pairing or Instances page searched again, so the other instance vanished until somebody opened BombVault on either box. Every member address is now asked again every two and a half minutes.
- **A container backed up config only shows its last backup** on the dashboard and in its row instead of Never ([#277](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/277)). Such a backup saves the container's definition and makes no restic snapshot, and the date was taken from snapshots only.

## 🌐 Translations

- The new pairing windows, the password warning and the Instances texts in all 42 languages.
- The pairing section of the off-site recovery page in all 26 documentation languages.

## Upgrading

- **Nothing has to be changed.** Settings, the pairing group and the relay carry over as they are.
- **Pairing is under Settings, System** now. A bookmark to the old Pairing tab under Instances still leads there.
- **An instance without a login password** shows the password warning on its phrase card until you set one.
